topic: Malaysia: coalition politics, political transitions, and post-2018 electoral change
scope_decisions: The set stays focused on federal coalition politics from GE14 through the post-GE15 settlement.
It treats government changes in 2020 and 2021 as parliamentary realignments rather than as fresh electoral mandates.
Regional blocs are included because GPS and other East Malaysian actors became decisive in coalition arithmetic.
The artifact set uses stable coalition labels and avoids a state-election deep dive so the benchmark stays compact.
decisions: Keep the chronological boundary centered on 2018-2022 so the topic covers the whole post-GE14 transition arc.
Use qualitative language for seat arithmetic except where a source makes the majority condition clear.
Frame the anti-hopping law as institutional repair, not as a separate legal-history topic.
Use short Malay and Simplified Chinese markers only where they help extraction and remain historically plausible.
open_questions: Should a later canonical pass add a dedicated comparison with state-level coalition shifts in Sabah and Melaka, or keep the federal focus only?
Should the coalition map be extended to include more temporary 2020-2022 labels, or stay with the stable blocs used here?
Should future canonical output include exact seat totals for GE14 and GE15, or keep the current majority-and-hung-parliament framing?
open_uncertainty: Coalition labels changed quickly between 2020 and 2022, so the set uses the most stable high-level bloc names rather than every short-lived arrangement.
Different summaries present the 2020-2021 transition with slightly different emphasis, so the prose keeps the parliamentary majority test central and avoids over-specific personality disputes.
Exact seat totals are omitted in the prose and tables because the benchmark only needs the structural change from dominant-party rule to coalition bargaining.
